svg.title: 65 years of NAD+ drips and shots, and what the controlled tests found
svg.desc: Timeline. 1961: Two short preliminary reports: NAD (then DPN) for addiction. 1966: Hoffer: NAD tablets make schizophrenia patients well in days. 1967: Double-blind test in 20 patients: no better than placebo. 1973: Psychiatrists’ task force: the NAD claims were refuted. 1994: Double-blind NADH drips in Parkinson’s: no difference. 2001: Louisiana clinic says it starts IV NAD addiction detox. 2017: FDA advisers vote not to put NAD on the compounding list. 2018: 1-page abstract: 8 people aged 70–80, no control group. 2019: FDA proposes not listing NAD; no final rule since. Feb 2026: Clinic records: all 6 NAD+ drip clients had cramps, nausea. Oct 8, 2026: Oral NR does worse than placebo in 410 Parkinson’s patients. Oct 14, 2026: Company NR-shot study: no placebo group.
